_doc: Revert-verify mutants for the EPIPE guard added in #4436 (round-1 review). These axes judge the guard's BRANCHES in-process; the delivered effect — a real child, a real pipe, a reader that leaves — is axis S7 in set-body-4436.pipe.spec.json. Both are needed and neither subsumes the other: the harness cannot reach the rethrow branch (set-body has no reachable non-EPIPE stdio error), and these cannot prove the process survives. ⛔ Like its siblings this spec runs LOCALLY and under the mutant driver, NOT in CI (verify-harness-runner's DIRS covers ~/dotfiles only, and the CLI jest job runs the tests but no mutants). Expectations written BEFORE the run.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/cli/src/utils/stdioClosedReader.ts

G1_condition_inverted._note: Swaps which errors survive: EPIPE would be rethrown (the crash the guard exists to prevent) and a genuine stdio failure would be swallowed. Reddens both swallow axes and the rethrow axis; E4 (listener count) stays green, which is what shows E4 measures installation and not behaviour.

G2_idempotence_flag_removed._note: Every call would add another listener. Only E4 reddens — the behaviour axes pass with N listeners just as with one, which is exactly why the accumulation would go unnoticed until MaxListenersExceeded in a long-lived process or a jest worker running many suites.

G3_swallow_everything._note: The over-broad form: silence EVERY stdio error, not just the closed reader. E1/E2 stay green (EPIPE is still swallowed) and only E3 reddens — the axis that keeps the guard narrow. Without E3 this mutant would be invisible, and a real stdio failure would disappear.
